revision.text:
{{神社| 名称=神明神社| 所在地=岡山県総社市福井字神明240| 位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|41|00|N|133|45|13|E|scale:25000}}| 祭神=天照皇大神 豊受大神| 社格=| 創建=不明| 例祭=[[10月第3日曜日]] }}
'''神明神社'''（しんめいじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[総社市]]福井にある[[神社]]である。[[天照大神]] [[豊受大神]]を祀る。
==歴史==
備中風土記の逸文では、伊勢御神の社の東に河あり。宮瀬川と名づく。河の西は、吉備建日子命の宮なりき。此の三世の王の宮を造りし故に、仍りて宮瀬と名づく。
日本古典文学大系２・風土記では、伊勢御神社を総社市福井の神明神社に擬する説があるが確かではない。天照大神を祭る社と記載されている。
また元伊勢伝承として、いくつかの文献に記載がある。
==末社==
荒神社
地神社
金神神社
木本宮・正殿宮
七社宮
==文献==
延喜式神名帳頭註 (1503年) 卜部(吉田)兼倶
諸社根元記 (1530年～1540年頃)
諸神記 (1543年)
神祇志料 栗田 寛
吉備郡史 永山卯三郎
弐拾弐社明細書 (明治７年 式外古社) 堀 安道
吉備郡神社誌 (古郡神社の項) 高杉槌蔵
吉備回廊 (山陽新聞 平成8年4月14日掲載) 山陽新聞社
== 交通 ==
* 鉄道：[[西日本旅客鉄道|JR西日本]][[吉備線]]・[[東総社駅]]下車。北に徒歩約10分。

日本古典文学大系２・風土記では、伊勢御神社を総社市福井の神明神社に擬する説があるが確かではない。天照大神を祭る社と記載されている。
また元伊勢『名方浜宮』として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。
現在は単立神社として存続している。

備中風土記の逸文『宮瀬川』では、伊勢御神の社の東に河あり。宮瀬川と名づく。河の西は、吉備建日子命の宮なりき。此の三世の王の宮を造りし故に、仍りて宮瀬と名づく。
日本古典文学大系２・風土記では、伊勢御神社を総社市福井の神明神社に擬する説があるが確かではない。天照大神を祭る社と記載されている。
また元伊勢『名方浜宮』として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。
現在は単立神社として存続している。

==歴史==
備中風土記の逸文『宮瀬川』では、伊勢御神の社の東に河あり。宮瀬川と名づく。河の西は、吉備建日子命の宮なりき。此の三世の王の宮を造りし故に、仍りて宮瀬と名づく。日本古典文学大系2・風土記では、伊勢御神社を総社市福井の神明神社に擬する説があるが確かではない。天照大神を祭る社と記載されている。また元伊勢『名方浜宮』として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。現在は単立神社として存続している。
==末社== *荒神社 *地神社 *金神神社 *木本宮・正殿宮 *七社宮
==文献== *延喜式神名帳頭註（1503年）吉田文庫 卜部（吉田）兼倶著 『宮瀬川』 *諸社根元記（1530年～1540年頃）『宮瀬川』 *諸神記（1543年）『宮瀬川』 *神祇志料 思文閣 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *古風土記逸文考証 有峰書店 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *上代歴史地理新考 山陽道/備中国・宮瀬川 三省堂 井上通泰著『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡史 名著出版 永山卯三郎著 『名方浜宮』 *弐拾弐社明細書（明治7年 式外古社）岡山県社寺掛（編）『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *備中国賀陽郡神社明細帳（明治22年2月）賀陽郡役所 『名方浜宮』 *大日本地名辞典（明治33年）冨書房 吉田東伍著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡神社誌（古郡神社の項）岡山県神職会吉備支部 高杉槌蔵著『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *月刊歴史手帖/古代吉備豪族の誕生（1976年4卷6号）名著出版 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *岡山県埋蔵文化財発掘調査報告書35/備中こうもり塚古墳 岡山県教育委員会 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承と造山古墳（吉備されど吉備）古代吉備国を語る会 出宮徳尚著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承（弐）吉備地方文化研究第19号 就実大学吉備地方文化研究所 出宮徳尚著 *総社市史 通史編・古代中世史料編・考古資料編（備中風土記の項）総社市『宮瀬川』 *吉備回廊（山陽新聞 平成8年4月14日掲載）山陽新聞社『宮瀬川』
== 交通 == * 鉄道：[[西日本旅客鉄道|JR西日本]][[吉備線]]・[[東総社駅]]下車。北に徒歩約10分。
== 外部リンク == * [http://www.megaegg.ne.jp/~shinmei 神明神社（公式サイト）]

'''神明神社'''（しんめいじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[総社市]]福井字神明240にある[[神社]]である。かつては、[[備中国]][[賀陽郡]][[阿部村]]（アブムラ）（現[[岡山県]][[総社市]]福井の南部）の氏神であった。[[阿部村]]（アブムラ）は、[[1881年]]（[[明治]]14年）に福井村と合併して福井村となる。 ==概要== [[神明神社 (総社市)]]は、[[天照大神]]を祭神とし、[[伊勢神宮]][[内宮]]を総本社とする神社である。[[神使]]は[[鶏]]である。[[天岩戸]]で[[鶏]]（長鳴鳥）を鳴かせ[[天照大神]]を誘い出したことは広く知られている。 ==風土記逸文== [[備中国]][[風土記]]逸文である『[[宮瀬川]]』（みやせがわ）によると、[[賀陽郡]]に『伊勢御神社』（いせのみかみのやしろ）の東に河があり、河の西に『吉備建日子命宮』（きびたけひこのみことのみや）があるので、この河を『[[宮瀬川]]』と称した、とある。この『伊勢御神社』を、[[神明神社 (総社市)]]に比定する説もあるが、確かなことはわからない。また元伊勢[[名方浜宮]]として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。現在は単立神社として存続している。 ==末社== *荒神社 *地神社 *金神神社 *木本宮・正殿宮 *七社宮 ==文献== *延喜式神名帳頭註（1503年）吉田文庫 卜部（吉田）兼倶著 『宮瀬川』 *諸社根元記（1530年～1540年頃）『宮瀬川』 *諸神記（1543年）『宮瀬川』 *神祇志料 思文閣 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *古風土記逸文考証 有峰書店 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *上代歴史地理新考 山陽道/備中国・宮瀬川 三省堂 井上通泰著『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡史 名著出版 永山卯三郎著 『名方浜宮』 *弐拾弐社明細書（明治7年 式外古社）岡山県社寺掛（編）『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *備中国賀陽郡神社明細帳（明治22年2月）賀陽郡役所 『名方浜宮』 *大日本地名辞典（明治33年）冨書房 吉田東伍著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡神社誌（古郡神社の項）岡山県神職会吉備支部 高杉槌蔵著『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *月刊歴史手帖/古代吉備豪族の誕生（1976年4卷6号）名著出版 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *岡山県埋蔵文化財発掘調査報告書35/備中こうもり塚古墳 岡山県教育委員会 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承と造山古墳（吉備されど吉備）古代吉備国を語る会 出宮徳尚著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承（弐）吉備地方文化研究第19号 就実大学吉備地方文化研究所 出宮徳尚著 *総社市史 通史編・古代中世史料編・考古資料編（備中風土記の項）総社市『宮瀬川』 *吉備回廊（山陽新聞 平成8年4月14日掲載）山陽新聞社『宮瀬川』 == 関連項目 == *[[伊勢神宮]] *[[内宮]] *[[天照大神]] *[[風土記]] *[[宮瀬川]] *[[阿部村]] *[[大森検校城誉]] *[[堀安道]]
== 交通 == * 鉄道：[[西日本旅客鉄道|JR西日本]][[吉備線]]・[[東総社駅]]下車。北に徒歩約10分。

備中国[[風土記]]逸文である『[[宮瀬川]]』（みやせがわ）によると、賀陽郡に『伊勢御神社』（いせのみかみのやしろ）の東に河があり、河の西に『吉備建日子命宮』（きびたけひこのみことのみや）があるので、この河を『宮瀬川』と称した、とある。この『伊勢御神社』を、神明神社に比定する説もあるが、確かなことはわからない。また元伊勢名方浜宮として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。
現在は単立神社として存続している。
==末社== *荒神社 *地神社 *金神神社 *木本宮・正殿宮 *七社宮
==文献== *延喜式神名帳頭註（1503年）吉田文庫 卜部（吉田）兼倶著 『宮瀬川』 *諸社根元記（1530年～1540年頃）『宮瀬川』 *諸神記（1543年）『宮瀬川』 *神祇志料 思文閣 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *古風土記逸文考証 有峰書店 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *上代歴史地理新考 山陽道/備中国・宮瀬川 三省堂 井上通泰著『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡史 名著出版 永山卯三郎著 『名方浜宮』 *弐拾弐社明細書（明治7年 式外古社）岡山県社寺掛（編）『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *備中国賀陽郡神社明細帳（明治22年2月）賀陽郡役所 『名方浜宮』 *大日本地名辞典（明治33年）冨書房 吉田東伍著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡神社誌（古郡神社の項）岡山県神職会吉備支部 高杉槌蔵著『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *月刊歴史手帖/古代吉備豪族の誕生（1976年4卷6号）名著出版 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *岡山県埋蔵文化財発掘調査報告書35/備中こうもり塚古墳 岡山県教育委員会 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承と造山古墳（吉備されど吉備）[[古代吉備国を語る会]] 出宮徳尚著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承（弐）吉備地方文化研究第19号 就実大学吉備地方文化研究所 出宮徳尚著 *総社市史 通史編・古代中世史料編・考古資料編（備中風土記の項）総社市『宮瀬川』 *吉備回廊（山陽新聞 平成8年4月14日掲載）山陽新聞社『宮瀬川』
== 交通 == * 鉄道：[[西日本旅客鉄道|JR西日本]][[吉備線]]・[[東総社駅]]下車。北に徒歩約10分。

'''神明神社'''（しんめいじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[総社市]]にある[[神社]]である。
== 概要 == かつては[[備中国]][[賀陽郡]][[阿部村 (岡山県)|阿部村]]（あぶむら）<ref>現在の岡山県総社市福井の南部。[[1881年]]（[[明治]]14年）に福井村と合併して福井村となる。</ref>の氏神で、[[天照大神]]を祭神とし、[[伊勢神宮]][[内宮]]を本社とする。[[神使]]は、[[天岩戸]]で天照大神を誘い出したことで知られる[[鶏]]（長鳴鳥）である。
備中国[[風土記]]逸文である『[[宮瀬川]]』（みやせがわ）によると、賀陽郡に『伊勢御神社』（いせのみかみのやしろ）の東に河があり、河の西に『吉備建日子命宮』（きびたけひこのみことのみや）があるので、この河を『宮瀬川』と称した、とある。この『伊勢御神社』を、神明神社に比定する説もあるが、確かなことはわからない。また元伊勢名方浜宮として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。
現在は単立神社として存続している。

{{神社 |名称=神明神社 |画像={{画像募集中|cat=総社市}} |所在地=岡山県総社市福井字神明240 |位置={{Coord|34|41|00|N|133|45|13|E|scale:25000|display=inline,title}} |祭神=[[天照大神]] |社格= |創建=不明 |本殿=[[流造]] |例祭=10月第3日曜日 |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Okayama Prefecture|label=神明神社|float=center|relief=1|width=256}} }} '''神明神社'''（しんめいじんじゃ）は、[[岡山県]][[総社市]]にある[[神社]]である。
== 概要 == かつては[[備中国]][[賀陽郡]][[阿部村 (岡山県)|阿部村]]（あぶむら）<ref>現在の岡山県総社市福井の南部。[[1881年]]（[[明治]]14年）に福井村と合併して福井村となる。</ref>の氏神で、[[天照大神]]を祭神とし、[[伊勢神宮]][[皇大神宮|内宮]]を本社とする。[[神使]]は、[[天岩戸]]で天照大神を誘い出したことで知られる[[鶏]]（長鳴鳥）である。
備中国[[風土記]]逸文である『[[宮瀬川]]』（みやせがわ）によると、賀陽郡に『伊勢御神社』（いせのみかみのやしろ）の東に河があり、河の西に『吉備建日子命宮』（きびたけひこのみことのみや）があるので、この河を『宮瀬川』と称した、とある。この『伊勢御神社』を、神明神社に比定する説もあるが、確かなことはわからない。また元伊勢名方浜宮として、いくつかの文献に記載が残る。
現在は単立神社として存続している。
==末社== *荒神社 *地神社 *金神神社 *木本宮・正殿宮 *七社宮
==文献== *延喜式神名帳頭註（1503年）吉田文庫 卜部（吉田）兼倶著 『宮瀬川』 *諸社根元記（1530年～1540年頃）『宮瀬川』 *諸神記（1543年）『宮瀬川』 *神祇志料 思文閣 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *古風土記逸文考証 有峰書店 栗田寛著 『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *上代歴史地理新考 山陽道/備中国・宮瀬川 三省堂 井上通泰著『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡史 名著出版 永山卯三郎著 『名方浜宮』 *弐拾弐社明細書（明治7年 式外古社）岡山県社寺掛（編）『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *備中国賀陽郡神社明細帳（明治22年2月）賀陽郡役所 『名方浜宮』 *大日本地名辞典（明治33年）冨書房 吉田東伍著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備郡神社誌（古郡神社の項）岡山県神職会吉備支部 高杉槌蔵著『名方浜宮』『宮瀬川』 *月刊歴史手帖/古代吉備豪族の誕生（1976年4卷6号）名著出版 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *岡山県埋蔵文化財発掘調査報告書35/備中こうもり塚古墳 岡山県教育委員会 葛原克人著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承と造山古墳（吉備されど吉備）[[古代吉備国を語る会]] 出宮徳尚著 『宮瀬川』 *吉備津彦伝承（弐）吉備地方文化研究第19号 就実大学吉備地方文化研究所 出宮徳尚著 *総社市史 通史編・古代中世史料編・考古資料編（備中風土記の項）総社市『宮瀬川』 *吉備回廊（山陽新聞 平成8年4月14日掲載）山陽新聞社『宮瀬川』
== 交通 == * 鉄道：[[西日本旅客鉄道|JR西日本]]桃太郎線（[[吉備線]]）・[[東総社駅]]下車。北に徒歩約10分。
==脚注== {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}}
== 関連項目 == *[[大森検校城誉]] *[[堀安道]]

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

* **Rail:** Approximately 10 minutes on foot north from [[JR West Japan|JR West]] [[:en:Momotarō Line|Momotarō Line]] ([[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]) at [[:en:Higashi-Sōja Station|Higashi-Sōja Station]].

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

* **Rail:** Approximately 10 minutes on foot north from [[JR West Japan|JR West]] [[:en:Momotarō Line|Momotarō Line]] ([[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]) at [[:en:Higashi-Sōja Station|Higashi-Sōja Station]].

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

* **Rail:** Approximately 10 minutes on foot north from [[JR West Japan|JR West]] [[:en:Momotarō Line|Momotarō Line]] ([[:en:Kibi Line|Kibi Line]]) at [[:en:Higashi-Sōja Station|Higashi-Sōja Station]].

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], [[:en:Okayama Prefecture|Okayama Prefecture]], Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In [[:en:1881|1881]] (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the [[:en:Chicken|Chicken]] (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)
* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

== Sub-Shrines==
* Kōjin Shrine (荒神社)
* Ji Shrine (地神社)
* Kin Shrine (金神神社)
* Kimoto Shrine & Shōden Shrine (木本宮・正殿宮)

== Historical Records==

er |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)

'''Shinmei Shrine''' (神明神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in [[:en:Sōja, Okayama|Sōja City]], {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture|WD=Q132936|lt=Okayama Prefecture|1=Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview==
The shrine was historically the tutelary deity of [[Abe Village (Okayama)|Abe Village]] (阿部村) in [[Kayo District, Bitchū Province|Kayo District, Bitchū Province]].<ref>Abe Village was located in what is now southern Fukui, Sōja City. In {{ill|1881|en|1881|WD=Q7808|lt=1881|1=1881}} (Meiji 14), it merged with Fukui Village.</ref> The enshrined deity is [[Amaterasu]], and the shrine is associated with the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], specifically the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine). 

The shrine’s sacred messenger is the {{ill|Chicken|en|Chicken|WD=Q780|lt=Chicken|1=Chicken}} (long-crowing bird), which played a role in luring Amaterasu out of the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (Heavenly Rock Cave).

An excerpt from the lost [[Fudoki]] of Bitchū Province, titled *Miyasegawa* (宮瀬川), states that in Kayo District, there was a river to the east of the *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* (伊勢御神社), and to the west of the river stood the *Kibi Takehiko no Mikoto no Miya* (吉備建日子命宮). This river was thus called *Miyasegawa*. Some theories equate *Ise Mikami no Yashiro* with Shinmei Shrine, though this remains uncertain. Additionally, records indicate that the shrine was known as *Motoise Nakatahama Shrine* in several historical texts.

Today, the shrine operates independently.

* Ji Shrine (地神社)

* Nanasha Shrine (七社宮)
